Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:10:1.english: [It] teaches - trenches and [water] channels first.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:10:2.english: And then explains - From where they are derived.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:11:1.english: That it is constricted and round - Short and round.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:13:1.hebrew: אבל חריצין - דרחבין ולא מטללי, אימא לא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:13:1.english: But [concerning] trenches - Since they are wide and not covered, I would say not.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:15:1.hebrew: לאו משום דלית ביה חבט - ואע"ג דאית ביה הבל, וקשיא לתרוייהו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:15:1.english: Is it not because there is no impact in it - Even though there are fumes in it, and [this] is a difficulty for both of them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:16:1.hebrew: לא משום דלית ביה הבלא - וכ"ש דחבטה לית ליה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:16:1.english: No, because there are no fumes in it - And all the more so that it has no [fatal] impact.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:16:2.english: To [cause] damage - [It] became ill because of the fumes and grew weak.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:17:2.hebrew: דדלאי - משקה שדות, והיא עמוקה אמה, ולפיכך היא נקראת אמת המים, דעמוקה אמה ורחבה אמה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:17:2.english: Of water-drawers [dedala’ei] - [For] irrigating fields, and it is one cubit deep; and therefore it is called an amat hamayim [water channel; literally, a cubit of water], because it is one cubit deep and one cubit wide.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:17:3.hebrew: טרפיה רב נחמן - משום ריסוקי אברים, דהיא אחת מי"ח טריפות דתנן (חולין דף מב.): נפלה מן הגג, ואע"פ דלא חזינן ביה מכה אלא שאין יכול לעמוד. ואמרינן התם (דף נא:): אם שהתה מעת לעת ושחטה, כשירה; ואם עמדה והלכה, אינה צריכה מעת לעת; ושור זה לא עמד:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:17:3.english: Rav Naḥman deemed it tereifah - Because of crushing of the limbs [internal organs], for it is one of the eighteen tereifot, as we learned in a Mishnah (Chullin 42a): "[If an animal] fell from the roof" — even though we do not see a wound on it, only that it cannot stand. And we say there (51b): "If it survived twenty-four hours and one slaughtered it, it is kosher; and if it stood up and walked, it does not require twenty-four hours." And this ox did not stand [up].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:18:1.hebrew: קבא דקמחא - להוצאותיו, עד שיבא לפני חכמים לשאול ויורוהו: אם שהתה מעת לעת ושחטה, כשירה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:18:1.english: A kav of flour - For his expenses, until he comes before the Sages to ask and they instruct him: if [the ox] remained [alive] for twenty-four hours and he slaughtered it, [it is] fit [to eat].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:18:2.english: He would not have lost - For he would have waited.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:1:1.hebrew: ארך אף - משמע מאריך רוגז וממתין מליפרע. ארך אפים משמע שני רצונים, אחת של טובה ואחת של רעה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:1:1.english: Erekh af - implies [that He] prolongs anger and waits before exacting punishment. Erekh appayim implies two dispositions: one of good and one of evil.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:1:2.english: For the righteous - [He refrains] from paying [their] good reward immediately.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:1:3.english: And for the wicked - [He refrains] from exacting punishment from them immediately.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:2:1.english: He should not clear stones - [That is,] to clear away stones.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:2:2.english: Into your property - The public domain is his all his days.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:2:3.english: From property that is not yours - Perhaps you are destined to sell it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:2:4.english: He mocked him - He did not understand the reason for the matter.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:4:1.hebrew: חריצין ונעיצין - בור עגול הוא. שיח ארוכה וקצרה. מערה מרובעת ומכוסה בקרוי, אלא שיש לה פה. חריצין רחבין ומרובעין כמערה ואינן מקורין, אלא כל פיו פתוח:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:4:1.english: Trenches [charitzin] and channels [ne'itzin] - A pit [bor] is round. A ditch [shiach] is long and narrow. A cave [me'arah] is square and covered with a roof, except that it has an opening. Trenches [charitzin] are wide and square like a cave and are not roofed; rather, their entire opening is open.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:4:2.english: Ne'itzin - [They are] narrow at the bottom and wide at the top.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:4:4.hebrew: מה בור שיש בו כדי להמית - דהיינו י' טפחים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:4:4.english: Just as a pit that has sufficient [depth] to cause death - That is, ten handbreadths.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:5:1.hebrew: להבלו - משום דעבד ליה הבל לבור, ולא משום חבטו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:5:1.english: For its fumes - Because he created fumes in the pit, and not because of its impact.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:5:2.english: Ground of the world - And it is not his.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:6:1.hebrew: שמואל אמר להבלו - חייבה תורה כדקאמרינן, ואע"ג דהבלא ממילא אתי ליה, וכ"ש לחבטו, דאיהו עבד ליה חבטה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:6:1.english: Shmuel said: For its fumes - the Torah rendered [one] liable, as we say, even though the fumes come about on their own; and all the more so for its impact, since he [himself] caused the impact.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:6:2.hebrew: ואם תאמר - דוקא לחבטו ולא להבלו, דהא ממילא הוא ואיהו לא עבדיה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:6:2.english: And if you say - [that the Torah spoke] specifically regarding its impact and not regarding its fumes, because [the fumes] come about on their own and he did not make them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:6:3.english: The Torah testifies about a pit - For "a pit" is written without qualification.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:6:4.english: And even [a pit] full of woolen sponges - For there is no impact.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:7:1.hebrew: מאי בינייהו - מכדי, היכא דמת בו, בין לרב בין לשמואל חייב. ואפילו נבקעת כריסו או נשברה מפרקתו, מחייב נמי רב, דאיכא למימר הבלא נמי קטלתיה. ואפי' נשברה רגלו וכיחש, איכא למימר מחמת הבל הבור חלה וכיחש. מה לי אי טעמא דחיובא משום חבטה, מה לי משום הבל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:7:1.english: What [is the difference] between them - After all, wherever [an animal] died in it, both according to Rav and according to Shmuel [the owner of the pit] is liable. And even if its belly burst or its neck broke, Rav also holds [him] liable, for one can say [that] the fumes also killed it. And even if its leg broke and it grew weak, one can say [that] it fell ill and grew weak because of the fumes of the pit. What difference is it to me if the reason for liability is because of impact, [and] what difference is it to me [if it is] because of fumes?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:7:2.hebrew: דעבד גובה - תל גבוה עשרה ברה"ר, ועלה שם שור ונפל, דהכא ליכא הבלא אלא חבט:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:7:2.english: Where [one] made a mound - A mound ten [handbreadths] high in the public domain, and an ox climbed up there and fell; for here there are no fumes, only impact.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:8:1.hebrew: דרך נפילה - בעומק משמע, ועל פניו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50b:8:1.english: [The] manner of falling - [This] implies into a depth, and upon its face.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50b:10:1.hebrew: תני והדר מפרש - פי': תני והדר מפרש מהיכא נפקא לן:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50b:10:1.english: [It] teaches and then explains - Explanation: [it] teaches [the law] and then explains from where we derive it.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50b:18:1.hebrew: אם שהתה מעת לעת ושחטה כשירה - בפרק אלו טריפות (חולין נא: ושם) אומר: עמדה — אין צריכה מעת לעת, בדיקה ודאי בעי; הלכה — אפילו בדיקה לא בעי. אבל כששהתה מעת לעת — אין להוכיח משם אי בעי בדיקה אי לא. ומתוך ה"ג משמע דבעי בדיקה, שפירש: אנן לא בקיאינן בבדיקה, ולדידן בעי י"ב חדש:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50b:18:1.english: "If it remained [alive] for twenty-four hours and one slaughtered it, it is fit [to eat]" - In the chapter [entitled] Eilu Tereifot (Chullin 51b, and ad loc.), [the Gemara] says: [If] it stood up, it does not require twenty-four hours, [but] it certainly requires an examination; [if] it walked, it does not even require an examination. However, when it remained [alive] for twenty-four hours, one cannot prove from there whether it requires an examination or not. And from Halakhot Gedolot it is implied that it requires an examination, for it explained: We are not expert in examination, and for us it requires twelve months.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50b:1:1.hebrew: ארך אפים לצדיקים ולרשעים - בעושין פסין (עירובין דף כב. ושם) משמע לרשעים להאבידם מן העוה"ב, ובחלק (סנהדרין דף קיא.) משמע לטובה. וי"ל: כשאין סופו לעשות תשובה — הוא לרעה, אבל בסופו לעשות תשובה — הוא לטובה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50b:1:1.english: Long-suffering for the righteous and for the wicked - In [the chapter] Osin Passin (Eruvin 22a and elsewhere), it implies [that He is long-suffering] for the wicked in order to destroy them from the World to Come, whereas in [the chapter] Chelek (Sanhedrin 111a), it implies [that it is] for good. And one can answer: when [a person] will not ultimately repent, it is for harm, whereas when [he] will ultimately repent, it is for good.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50b:7:1.hebrew: איכא בינייהו דעבד גובה - ה"נ הוה מצי למימר דנפל דרך אחוריו, דלרב לא מיחייב אלא דרך פניו דאיכא הבל; אי נמי בבור שרחבה יותר על עומקה דליכא הבל, כדאמרינן (לקמן בבא קמא נא:), וחדא נקט:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50b:7:1.english: "The difference between them is where one fashioned a mound" - Similarly, [the Gemara] could have said [the difference is] where [an animal] fell backward, for according to Rav one is only liable [when it falls] face-first, where there are fumes; or alternatively, in [the case of] a pit whose width is greater than its depth, where there are no fumes, as we say (later, Bava Kamma 51b) — and it [simply] cited one [example].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50b:7:2.hebrew: לשמואל אגובה נמי מיחייב - ע"כ בנתקל בגובה ונחבט בקרקע; דאי בנחבט בגובה, מודה רב דחייב, כמו באבנו וסכינו ומשאו, דאמר (לעיל בבא קמא דף ג.): אי דאפקריה, בין לרב בין לשמואל היינו בור, והיינו משום דחבטה דידיה הוא. וקשה: דבנתקל בגובה ונחבט בקרקע מודה שמואל דפטור, דקרקע עולם הזיקתו, כדמוכח לקמן (בבא קמא דף נג.): אמר שמואל היכי דמי לאחוריו דפטור? כגון שנתקל בבור ונפל אחורי הבור. וי"ל: כגון דעבד גובה ה' טפחים, וסביב הגובה חפר בעומק ה' טפחים, ונתקל בגובה ונחבט בעומק בור. א"נ: דוקא התם גבי נפל מקול הכרייה פטר שמואל, שקול הכרייה גרם לו ליפול, וחבטה נמי לא גרם לו מעשיו, שנחבט בקרקע שחוץ לבור. ואין להקשות דליחייב בעל הבור החצי שעשה חצי התקלה, ובכל נמי ליחייב — דהא מוקי לה כרבי נתן, דכי ליכא לאישתלומי מהאי משתלם מהאי; י"ל דקסבר שמואל שאין לחייב בעל הבור לעולם, אפי' לרבי נתן, אלא כשעשה כל התקלה — אז יתחייב בעל הבור כשנחבט, ואפי' נחבט בקרקע עולם — או כשעשה ההיזק, אע"ג שלא עשה התקלה, אבל בחצי התקלה לא יתחייב בור כשנחבט בקרקע עולם. ולפי זה אתי שפיר הא דמשמע לקמן (שם): נתקל באבן ונפל לבור, דמחייב בעל האבן אע"ג דהאי בור לאו איהו כרייה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50b:7:2.english: [According] to Shmuel, he is also liable for a mound - Perforce [this is speaking] of one who stumbles on the mound and is dashed against the ground [below]; for if [it were speaking] of one who is dashed against the mound [itself], Rav would concede that he is liable, just as with his stone, his knife, and his burden, where [the Gemara] says (above, Bava Kamma 3a): if he renounced ownership of it, according to both Rav and Shmuel it is [categorized as] Pit — and that is because the impact is from his [own object]. And this is difficult: for in the case of one who stumbles on a mound and is dashed against the ground, Shmuel concedes that he is exempt, because the natural ground damaged it, as is proven below (Bava Kamma 53a): "Shmuel said: What is the case of 'behind it' where he is exempt? For example, where [an animal] stumbled on a pit and fell behind the pit." And one can answer: [it is] a case where he made a mound five handbreadths [high], and around the mound he dug to a depth of five handbreadths, so [the animal] stumbled on the mound and was dashed into the depth of the pit. Or alternatively: specifically there, regarding [an animal that] fell from the sound of the digging, did Shmuel exempt [him], because the sound of the digging caused it to fall, and as for the impact as well, his action did not cause it, since it was dashed against the ground outside the pit. And one should not object that the owner of the pit should be liable for half, since he made half of the obstacle — and he should even be liable for the whole, since [the Gemara] establishes it according to Rabbi Natan, that where one cannot collect from this one, one collects from the other — [for] one can say that Shmuel holds that the owner of the pit is never liable, even according to Rabbi Natan, unless he made the entire obstacle — then the owner of the pit is liable when [the animal] is dashed, even if it is dashed against the natural ground — or when he caused the actual damage, even though he did not make the obstacle; however, for half the obstacle, [the owner of] the pit is not liable when it is dashed against the natural ground. And according to this, it works out well — that which is implied below (ibid.): [where an animal] stumbled on a stone and fell into a pit, the owner of the stone is liable even though he did not dig this pit.
